newsitem.title: INDIA: Dalai Lama says Jiang could help over Tibet.
newsitem.headline: Dalai Lama says Jiang could help over Tibet.

text.p: Exiled Tibetan leader the Dalai Lama said China's new supreme leader Jiang Zemin could help resolve the Tibetan issue positively.

"Judging during the Tiananmen event, when he was mayor of Shanghai...he handled the demonstrations quite gently, and in a positive way. And that is an indication," the Dalai Lama told Reuters Television at his Indian headquarters in Dharamsala.

But Tibet's spiritual leader, who fled to India in 1959 after a failed anti-Chinese uprising in his homeland, said China's communist system could still thwart any efforts by Jiang even if he decided to make them.

"As for the totalitarian system which is constitutionalised with Marxist ideology, (with) one or two persons, it is difficult to change the system...But I always believe change will come," he said on Saturday.

The Dalai Lama paid tribute to Jiang's mentor, the late Deng Xiaoping, but said the former Chinese patriarch was a man of few words. "Of course he was one of the great new revolutionaries, and also I think in certain fields very diplomatic, and in certain fields very stubborn," the Dalai Lama said of the man he last met in Beijing in 1955.

Last week the Dalai Lama was quoted as voicing regreat that Deng had died without resolving questions over Tibet. Tibet was ruled by a theocratic Buddhist elite until 1950 when China's People's Liberation Army took over the area.
